title: Working with Joe Oliver: humour and relaxing the band
summary: Shoffner says Oliver was easy to work with, joked constantly, and had the band repeat one number until relaxed before making it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Yeah. For 14 years. I didn't know he was here that late. Well I was going to ask how Joe was to work with. Some people tell me he was a wonderful fellow. He was easy to get along with. And full of fun. And others talked like he was hard to work with.

Well the whole time I find that Joe was just like you say. Joe was an easy fellow to get along with. And he never did let you get tense. He never let you get tense. Yeah. Because he was joking the whole night long. That's what most people tell me. He just kept you in a good mood. You never got tense. You never got tense. If he see you come on the job and he, he didn't know about psychology but he was just gifted. Yeah.
You never got to get. Yeah. See he was, yeah see he was, yeah he was tight to you when he started telling some joke or started joking with you and first and last you'd be relaxed and all the way.

He was like, yeah. The same thing like if he started out and taking, playing the number like that. Now if he seen and he played the number the first time, he was tense, he allowed him to play that one number for 30 or 40 minutes. I said one number. Just keep on going, just keep it going over. Loosen up. Loosen up. So first and last you'd loosen up, loosen up and then he would knock out.
Then when you take the number again, everybody would be relaxed and just go over the number. And that's where we made all our numbers.
